faqs.question: What does JC-BK Virus DNA Detection by Real-Time PCR - EDTA Blood measure?
faqs.answer: This test detects the presence of two viruses, JC polyoma and BK virus.

faqs.question: Why is JC-BK Virus DNA Detection by Real-Time PCR - EDTA Blood done?
faqs.answer: • To detect infections caused by JC polyoma and BK viruses • To monitor and prevent complications such as kidney disease in immunocompromised individuals

faqs.question: When is JC-BK Virus DNA Detection test recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test is recommended for individuals who have • recently received an organ transplant or bone marrow transplant, • weak immune systems due to chemotherapy or other medications, • certain underlying conditions that affect the immune system, or • symptoms of acute infection caused by these viruses.

faqs.question: What if the results of the JC-BK Virus DNA Detection test are abnormal?
faqs.answer: If the test shows positive results indicating viral DNA, further testing may be required to detect the extent of infection and confirm the diagnosis.

faqs.question: What to expect during the JC-BK Virus DNA Detection test?
faqs.answer: This test involves drawing a sample of blood from your vein. The collected blood is sent to the laboratory for processing.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the JC-BK Virus DNA Detection test?
faqs.answer: If you are taking any medications or have any underlying medical conditions, inform your doctor. Also, tell them if you have any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the JC-BK Virus DNA Detection test?
faqs.answer: Viral culture testing: This test may be done to confirm the diagnosis after detecting viral DNA.

faqs.question: What is the JC-BK Virus DNA Detection by Real Time PCR - EDTA Blood also known as?
faqs.answer: JC-BK PCR test or Polyomavirus DNA Detection

faqs.question: What is immunodeficiency?
faqs.answer: Immunodeficiency refers to a weakened immune system that cannot adequately protect the body against infections and diseases. There are two types of immunodeficiency: primary immunodeficiency, which is inherited, and secondary immunodeficiency, which is caused by certain medical treatments or underlying conditions, such as HIV/AIDS.
